preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 200, representing the domain size of the function f.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.split()) == n + 1 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: The second line contains exactly n integers, each between 1 and n (inclusive), representing the function values f(1), f(2), ..., f(n).

postconditions.expression: stdout.isdigit() and (k := int(stdout)) >= 1 and k <= n
postconditions.description: The output is a positive integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ n) representing the minimum positive integer such that the k-th iterate of f, denoted f(k), is idempotent.

postconditions.expression: all((lambda f_k: all(f_k(f_k(x)) == f_k(x) for x in range(1, n + 1)))((lambda f: lambda x: f(x - 1))(lambda x: int(stdin.split()[x])))(int(stdout)) and any(not all(f_k(f_k(x)) == f_k(x) for x in range(1, n + 1)) for k in range(1, int(stdout)) if (f_k := (lambda f: lambda x: f(x - 1))(lambda x: int(stdin.split()[x])))(k))
postconditions.description: For the output k, the k-th iterate of f (f(k)) is idempotent (i.e., f(k)(f(k)(x)) = f(k)(x) for all x in {1, ..., n}), and no smaller positive integer k' satisfies this property.
